Transport and Merge: Cross-Architecture Merging for Large Language Models

Use activation correspondences to transfer knowledge between language models whose architectures do not match.

Cui Chenhang · Yang Binyun · Shen Fei · Chen Yuxin · Zheng Jingnan · Wang Xiang · Zhang An · Chua Tat-Seng

February 5, 2026 ·ICML 2026 ·Read the paper ·PDF ·Code
1Why this matters 2How it works 3What the study finds 4What this means

The short version

Transport and Merge uses optimal transport to infer cross-neuron correspondences from activations and guide weight-space fusion across heterogeneous models.

OTCross-neuron correspondence
CrossHeterogeneous model fusion
SmallShared-input alignment set

Why this matters

Conventional merging often assumes compatible architectures. That assumption limits transfer from high-resource source models to heterogeneous targets with limited task or language data.

How it works

  1. Collect activations from source and target models on a small set of shared inputs.
  2. Solve optimal transport to establish correspondences between heterogeneous neuronal representations.
  3. Use the resulting transport plans to guide direct weight-space fusion.

What the study finds

Experiments across low-resource languages and specialized domains report consistent improvements over the corresponding target models. The transfer uses a small input set to infer the cross-model correspondence.

What this means

Alignment is a prerequisite for meaningful cross-architecture fusion. Activation geometry offers a way to estimate that alignment instead of assuming matching neuron coordinates.
